subject: LGM non-convergence of quadratic or cubic slopes due to size of multiplier?

messages.author: 39f1ac78bd3926ba
messages.subject: LGM non-convergence of quadratic or cubic slopes due to size of multiplier?
parts:
Dear lavaan community,

I'm trying to run a series of latent growth models with different slopes, using questionnaire data from 10 measurement points. Specifically, I want to test a model with a linear slope, a model with linear and quadratic slope, and a model with a linear, quadratic, and cubic slope.

However, when I actually fitted this model (see below for general model specification), I got a non-convergence warning for the cubic model.  Then, when I remembered that actually, waves 6-10 are spaced 2 years apart rather than 1 (which was the case for waves 1-6) and adjusted the multipliers in the slopes to this, also the quadratic model gave me a non-convergence warning (whereas nothing else had changed).

My question now is whether it's possible that lavaan responds to the size of the multipliers for the slope indicators (which as you can see, go quite high for the quadratic and cubic slope, especially if I change the multipliers to indicate the longer time intervals between waves 6-10)? And if so, is there a way to solve this problem?

Many thanks in advance!

Sincerely,
Elisabeth

quadr.model <- '#growth model specification:
            i =~ 1*1neurot + 1*2neurot + 1*3neurot + 1*4neurot + 1*5neurot +
                 1*6neurot + 1*7neurot + 1*8neurot + 1*9neurot + 1*10neurot
           ls =~ 0*1neurot + 1*2neurot + 2*3neurot + 3*4neurot + 4*5neurot +
                 5*6neurot + 6*7neurot + 7*8neurot + 8*9neurot + 9*10neurot
           qs =~ 0*1neurot + 1*2neurot + 4*3neurot + 9*4neurot + 16*5neurot +
                 25*6neurot + 36*7neurot + 49*8neurot + 64*9neurot + 81*10neurot

            #time-invariant covariate:
            i ~ gender
           ls ~ gender
           qs ~ gender'
fit.quadr <- growth(quadr.model, data=data, estimator="MLR", missing="ML")
summary(fit.quadr, standardized=TRUE, rsquare=TRUE, fit.measures=TRUE)

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: LGM non-convergence of quadratic or cubic slopes due to size of multiplier?
parts: My question now is whether it's possible that lavaan responds to the size of the multipliers for the slope indicators (which as you can see, go quite high for the quadratic and cubic slope, especially if I change the multipliers to indicate the longer time intervals between waves 6-10)?
Possibly
is there a way to solve this problem?

You could reduce the size of the loadings by centering Time, so the latent intercept is the mean of somewhere in the middle of the occasions. For example, using the 7th occasion, the loadings would be like this (with 6-10 spaced 2 years apart)

ls =~ -7*1neurot + -6*2neurot + -5*3neurot + -4*4neurot + -3*5neurot +
                 -2*6neurot + 0*7neurot + 2*8neurot + 4*9neurot + 6*10neurot 

So now the occasions are coded -7 through +6, indicating how many years from the 7th wave.  Squaring these would only yield loadings from 0 to 49, but cubic would still be a huge range.

Better yet, R's contr.poly() function returns orthonormal contrast codes (i.e., variances = 1, so values are small), and you can customize the numerical values the codes are meant to represent (so they don't need to be equidistant).  Here's a script that capitalizes on lavaan accepting a character vector of model syntax, so it doesn't all need to be in a single string.

vars <- paste0(1:10, "neurot")
waves <- c(1:6, 8, 10, 12, 14)
orthoLoadings <- contr.poly(length(vars), scores = waves)
## first 3 columns are linear, quadratic, and cubic
orthoLoadings[ , 1:3]

## paste scripts together in components
mod.int <- c(paste0("i =~ 1*", vars),
             "i ~ gender")
mod.lin <- c(paste0("ls =~", orthoLoadings[ , ".L"], "*", vars), 
             "ls ~ gender")
mod.quadr <- c(paste0("qs =~", orthoLoadings[ , ".Q"], "*", vars), 
               "qs ~ gender")
mod.cub <- c(paste0("cs =~", orthoLoadings[ , ".C"], "*", vars), 
             "cs ~ gender")
## view all together
cat(c(mod.int, mod.lin, mod.quadr, mod.cub), sep = "\n")

## fit models
fit.int <- growth(mod.int,
data=data, estimator="MLR", missing="ML")
fit.lin <- growth(c(mod.int, mod.lin),
data=data, estimator="MLR", missing="ML")
fit.quadr <- growth(c(mod.int, mod.lin, mod.quadr),
data=data, estimator="MLR", missing="ML")
fit.cub <- growth(c(mod.int, mod.lin, mod.quadr, mod.cub),
data=data, estimator="MLR", missing="ML")

I hope that helps.

Terrence D. Jorgensen
Assistant Professor, Methods and Statistics
Research Institute for Child Development and Education, the University of Amsterdam

messages.subject: Re: LGM non-convergence of quadratic or cubic slopes due to size of multiplier?
parts: Thank you so much for thinking along, this is very helpful and allowed me to run all models without a problem.
Great!
does the use of these orthonormal contrast codes change the interpretation of the findings in any significant way that I should keep in mind?

Yes, the tests of linear, quadratic, etc. effects are valid, but you lose the simple interpretation of "a 1-unit increase in time is associated with an expected change of [slope] units in the outcome."  Essentially, the best way to interpret the results will be visually.  Pick your preferred model that balances complexity and parsimony, then calculate the expected marginal means for each timepoint (i.e., multiply the growth-factor means by the loading for each occasion).  If you store them in a vector, you can plot them against time.
